items.title: Eight Causes Behind Every Change — Including the Mind Switching Objects Mid-Thought

items.zh: 一、積時貯畜，二、他所損害，三、受用虧損，四、時節變異，五、火所焚燒，六、水所漂爛，七、風所鼓燥，八、異緣會遇。積時貯畜者，謂有色諸法，雖於好處安置守護，而經久時自然敗壞，其色衰損變異可得。他所損害者，謂種種色法，若為於他種種捶打、種種損害，即便種種形色變異。受用虧損者，謂各別屬主種種色物，受者受用增上力故，損減變異。時節變異者，謂秋冬時，叢林藥草華葉果等萎黃零落；於春夏時，枝葉華果青翠繁茂。火所焚燒者，謂大火縱逸，焚燒村邑、國城、王都，悉為灰燼。水所漂爛者，謂大水洪漫，漂蕩村邑、國城、王都，悉皆淪沒。風所鼓燥者，謂大風飄扇，濕衣、濕地、稼穡、叢林乾㬤枯槁。異緣
items.en: First, decay through long storage over accumulated time; second, harm from others; third, wearing down through use; fourth, seasonal change; fifth, destruction by fire; sixth, ruin by water; seventh, drying by wind; eighth, encountering a different condition … every change of every thing possessing form, and every thing lacking form, arises from precisely these eight causes — beyond these there is nothing further, nothing in excess.

items.zh: 會遇者，謂緣樂受觸，受樂受時，遇苦受觸；緣苦受觸，受苦受時，遇樂受觸；緣不苦不樂受觸，受不苦不樂受時，遇樂受觸、或苦受觸。又有貪者，會遇瞋緣，貪纏止息，發起瞋纏。如是有瞋、癡者，會遇異分煩惱生緣，當知亦爾。
items.en: Likewise, while eye-consciousness is presently active, if it encounters some other object or condition — a sound, a smell, a taste, a touch — a different, corresponding consciousness arises instead … and one who harbours craving, on encountering a condition that provokes anger, has their craving momentarily cease, and anger arise in its place. The same holds, one should know, for one who harbours anger or delusion encountering a condition provoking some other affliction.

items.zh: 如是眼識正現在前，會遇聲、香、味、觸境等餘境餘緣，起異分識。其餘一切，如理應知。是名八種變異因緣。一切有色及無色法所有變異，皆由如是八種因緣，除此更無若過若增。云何尋思內事分位所作變異無常之性？謂由觀見或自、或他，從少年位乃至老位，諸行相續前後差別，互不相似。見是事已，便作是念：如是諸行，其性無常。何以故？此內分位前後變異現可得故。云何尋思內事顯色所作變異無常之性？謂由觀見或自、或他，先有妙色，肌膚鮮澤；後見惡色，肌膚枯槁。復於後時，還見妙色，肌膚鮮澤。見是事已，便作是念：如是諸行，其性無常。何以故？此內顯色前後變異現可得故。云何尋思內事形色所作變異無常之性？謂如說顯色，如是形色由肥瘦故，應知亦爾。云何尋思內事興衰所作變異無常之性？謂由觀見或自、或他，先時眷屬財位，或見悉皆興盛；後見一切皆悉衰損。復於後時還見興盛。見是事已，便作是念：如是諸行，其性無常。何以故？興衰變異現可得故。云何尋思內事支節所作變異無常之性？謂由觀見或自、或他，先時支節無有缺減；後時觀見支節缺減。或王所作、或賊所作、或人所作、或非人作。見是事已，便作是念：如是諸行，其性無常。餘如前說。云何尋思內事劬勞所作變異無常之性？謂由觀見或自、或他，身疲勞性、身疲極性。或馳走所作、或跳踊所作、或趒躑所作、或騙騎所作、或作種種迅疾身業。復於餘時，見彼遠離疲勞疲極。見是事已，便作是念：如是諸行，其性無常。餘如前說。云何尋思內事他所損害所作變異無常之性？謂由觀見或自、或他，他所損害，其身變異。或由刀杖、鞭革、皮繩、矛矟等壞，或由種種蚊虻、蛇蝎諸惡毒觸之所損害。復於餘時，見不變異。見是事已，便作是念：如是諸行，其性無常。餘如前說。

blocks.text: Why things change, and the first of the fifteen observations of change in oneself. Most of today's Chinese (from 0471b27) is **untranslated**; the commentary summarises it.

"Decay through long storage; harm from others; wearing down through use; seasonal change; fire; water; wind (which dries); encountering a different condition." Venerable Miào Jìng on the first: "I put it in a locked cabinet, stored and protected", and still it decays. Master Cháng Bǎi on use: people stick name labels on their things, but use wears them out anyway.

The last cause applies to mind too: "while eye-consciousness is active, if it encounters a sound or smell, a different consciousness arises instead"; and "one who harbours craving, meeting a condition that provokes anger, has their craving momentarily replaced".

"Every change in form and formless things comes from these eight causes; there are no others." Then each of the fifteen changes is observed, always ending with the same reflection: "these formations are impermanent, because their change is directly seen." - **Life-stage**: oneself or another, from youth to old age, never the same. - **Complexion**: once fine and glowing, later withered, then fine again. - **Form**: fat and thin. - **Rise and decline**: family and wealth once flourishing, then ruined, then flourishing again. - **Limbs**: once whole, later lost, to kings, thieves, people, or spirits. - **Fatigue**: after running, leaping, riding; then rested again. - **Harm**: by knives, sticks, whips, mosquitoes, snakes, scorpions; then healed.

quiz.q: "One observes and sees (觀見), in oneself or another." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish 觀 and 見?
options: 見 is the eye's seeing, 觀 the mind's — the sixth consciousness
quiz.why: "One observes that, in oneself or in another, that from youth all the way to old age, these continuously arising factors show, from earlier to later, differences." Venerable Miào Jìng: 見 is seeing with the eye; 觀 is seeing with the mind — the sixth consciousness.

quiz.q: The seventh, "change from harm done by others" — what example does Venerable Miào Jìng give?
options: while chopping vegetables, suddenly cutting one's own finger
quiz.why: "Seventh, of harm done by others." Venerable Miào Jìng: when chopping vegetables, you mean to cut the vegetables and suddenly cut your own finger.

quiz.q: "Seventh, drying by wind (鼓燥)." What two functions of wind does Venerable Miào Jìng name?
quiz.why: "Seventh, drying by wind." Venerable Miào Jìng: wind has two functions — stirring and drying.

quiz.q: "First, 積時貯畜" — rendered "decay through accumulated time," dropping "storing." What do the lectures say?
options: Miào Jìng: locked away and protected, it still changes; Cháng Bǎi: change caused by time — given enough time, change is certain
quiz.why: "First, decay through accumulated time." Venerable Miào Jìng: I put it in a locked cabinet, stored and protected. Master Cháng Bǎi: this is change caused by time — given long enough, change is certain. The English omits "storing" (even what's carefully stored decays).

quiz.q: "Third, wearing down through use" — what example does Master Cháng Bǎi give?
options: a name sticker on a teacup soon peels up
quiz.why: "Third, wearing down through use." Master Cháng Bǎi: some people like to stick a name sticker on their teacup; before long it peels up.

quiz.q: "While eye-consciousness is active, encountering a sound … a different consciousness arises." What does Venerable Miào Jìng say?
options: see and hear at once equally
a sudden sound stops the eye-consciousness, and ear-consciousness starts
quiz.why: "While eye-consciousness is presently active, if it encounters some other object or condition — a sound, a smell, a taste, a touch — a different, corresponding consciousness arises instead." Venerable Miào Jìng: suddenly a particular sound appears, your eye-consciousness stops, and ear-consciousness starts up.

quiz.q: "Craving's 纏 ceases, anger's 纏 arises." How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain 纏?
options: affliction coils around you like a venomous snake
quiz.why: "One who harbours craving, on encountering a condition that provokes anger, has their craving momentarily cease, and anger arise in its place." Venerable Miào Jìng: when the affliction of craving comes, it's like a venomous snake coiling around you.
